alias_policy.description: SCML documents user-facing Linux syscall names while dispatch rows use the kernel's SYS_* constant spelling. Names in one alias group denote the same syscall ABI (e.g. sendfile/sendfile64, getpriority/get_priority, fstat/newfstat, newfstatat/fstatat). SCML coverage lookup tries the exact dispatch name first, then every other member of its alias group. The groups are reviewed pins in annotations.json, echoed into the generated metadata; a name with no exact or alias coverage is reported as absent, never silently treated as covered.

metadata.evidence_association: unsupported-success warnings anywhere in a syscall implementation file are associated with every handler defined in that file, because warnings frequently live in shared helpers and conversion impls (e.g. clone3 argument conversion in clone.rs) rather than in the handler body proper; each evidence site carries a scope field distinguishing handler-body evidence from file-level evidence

status_semantics.implemented: the handler resolves and the heuristic scan found no unsupported-success evidence in its implementation file; this is shallow handler-resolution evidence, not a Linux-compatibility claim
status_semantics.partial: the implementation file carries unsupported-success evidence (input warned away, ignored, or accepted without effect) on some path while the syscall still reports success
status_semantics.stub: the handler performs none of the requested effect: it returns ENOSYS on every path, or a reviewed annotation pin states that success is always reported without effect
status_semantics.unresolvable: the dispatch row references a handler that is not defined in the syscall source directory; always a coverage failure
